raw_response:
I am a 53-year-old woman who has been working this land since I was 18. Only finished primary school, so I don't read farming books or use those apps the young people talk about. I know what I know from doing it myself, from watching my neighbors, and from remembering what went wrong last year. My husband works at a construction site in Handan and only comes home on weekends. My son is married and lives in the county town with his wife. So it's mostly me and my 78-year-old mother-in-law at home, and she can't do heavy work anymore. I manage the 6 mu myself, with hired help when I absolutely need it.

I used to grow wheat and maize on all 6 mu, but six years ago my cousin's wife started growing stevia and made good money — the buyer comes right to the field with cash, no haggling at the grain station. I tried 1 mu first, then 2 mu, and now I keep 3 mu in stevia. It's hard work, more than grain, but the income is better and I need the cash. The other 3 mu I keep in wheat-maize, same as always, because we need the wheat for food and the maize feeds our pig.

**Wheat:** I planted the wheat last October in early October, right after the maize came off. I used saved seed mixed with a little new seed from the county store — about 15 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu and worked it in. Now it's March and the wheat is greening up. I will topdress with about 12 kg of urea per mu at jointing — I learned my lesson four years ago when I skipped it to save money, the heads were tiny and I lost almost a whole mu's worth. I irrigate wheat three times: once now at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Electricity for pumping costs money but wheat is our main food, so I don't cut here. I spray herbicide once in spring when the weeds are small. I do all the wheat work myself — 8 days of family labor. I expect about 380 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in early June, I have to plant maize fast — usually within two or three days, the window is always tight. I buy hybrid seed every year from the seed dealer, 50 yuan per mu, because saved seed doesn't work for hybrid. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow — because there's no time to come back later, the summer season is too short. I irrigate maize twice if the summer is dry, but usually the rains help some. I spray herbicide and sometimes insecticide if I see worms. This takes me about 6 days of family labor. I expect around 420 kg per mu.

**Stevia:** I plant stevia seedlings in mid-April. I buy the seedlings from the guy who comes to our village every spring — about 100 yuan per mu. Before planting I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I irrigate four times through the season. The first cut is in mid-July, then I dry the leaves under a plastic shed my husband helped me build. After the first cut I topdress with urea so the new branches grow strong. Second cut in mid-September, and another topdress. Maybe a small third cut in October before frost kills it. I spray herbicide twice and insecticide once if I see aphids. Stevia is very labor-heavy — planting, weeding, cutting, drying — so I hire two women from the village for 2 days each during the cutting season. It costs 120 yuan per day but I can't cut 3 mu fast enough by myself, and if the leaves get too old the buyer pays less. I do about 12 days of family labor on the stevia. I expect about 180 kg of dried leaves per mu if the weather is good.

My total costs this year are about 2,500 yuan. That's a lot for us, but my husband sends some money from his construction job, and I would rather spend enough on inputs than risk a bad year. I also keep about 800 yuan in cash hidden at home for emergencies — two years ago my mother-in-law got sick and the clinic wanted payment right away. I'm not buying more fertilizer than usual, even though some neighbors use more. I know what my land can do, and I'd rather be a little safe than sorry.
